# External source repos — index

Shallow (`--depth 1 --single-branch`) checkouts of the repos that ground finance-world.
**`.git` removed from every clone** — this is source, not history. Wave 1 cloned **2026-08-10**
(24 repos), wave 2 **2026-08-11** (+16 repos: the ERP-vendor axis, the ERP MCP census, and three
eval trees), wave 3 **2026-08-11** (+19 repos: the double-entry engine axis, the OCA
bank-reconciliation axis, and four first-party/vendor agent surfaces — see §8 and §9).
Total on disk: **1.3 GB** across **59 repos** — **well over** the ≤600 MB budget set in wave 1.
Four repos account for ~60% of it and all four have an obvious prune: `erp-bench` 215 MB (107 MB of
which is `tasks_ui/`, a byte-near-duplicate of `tasks/` differing only in `instruction.md` and
`task.toml`), `odoo` 205 MB (≥153 MB of which is `i18n/*.po` translation files — 100 MB in
`odoo/addons/base/i18n`, 53 MB in `addons/account/i18n`), `openbb` 233 MB (**140 MB is VCR test
cassettes** under `openbb_platform/providers/*/tests/record/` — 329 recorded `.yaml` HTTP
transcripts; `tmx` alone is 44 MB of tests against 248 KB of code) and `akaunting` 58 MB (36 MB
`public/`, of which 23 MB is compiled CSS). Pruning all four lands the corpus at ~750 MB with no
loss of research value; deferred until space bites. `.git` was removed from the wave-3 clones too
(verified: no `.git` at any depth under `repos/`).

**Six** repos are flagged `(sparse)` — they exceeded the ~150 MB clone cap (or carried a committed
`.venv`) but had a small, high-value subset, so they were taken as **partial clones**
(`--filter=blob:none --sparse`, non-cone excludes) with the excluded paths named in their row:
`financebench`, `tau2-bench`, `erpnext`, `d365-fasttrack-finance`, `FinMCP-Bench`, and wave-2's
`odoo`. Nothing else was modified.

> Licensing note for anyone lifting code (not facts) out of these. **Copyleft / restricted —
> facts only, never source:** `erpnext` (GPL-3.0), `sec-edgar-mcp` (AGPL-3.0), `odoo`
> (LGPL-3.0 — `odoo/LICENSE`, and `account`/`purchase` manifests declare LGPL-3),
> `opensuitemcp-netsuite` (**Sustainable Use License**, not OSI-approved —
> `opensuitemcp-netsuite/LICENSE`). **Permissive:** `mcp-erp-multivendor` and `valuecell` are
> Apache-2.0; `erp-bench` is **CC0-1.0** (`erp-bench/LICENSE`), the only wave-2 repo that is
> also a legal *code* source. **No LICENSE file at all:** `awesome-finance-mcp`,
> `odoo-ai-agent` (backend repo is private), `finance-agent-benchmark-bkl` (README badge says
> MIT, no file), plus the wave-1 unlicensed items noted in the tables. Everything else is
> MIT/Apache-2.0. Copying *tool names, schemas and workflow semantics* into our mocks is fine
> (interfaces/facts); copying source is not.
>
> **Wave-3 licence deltas — the copyleft share went up sharply, and one repo is not open source
> at all.** **Not OSI / source-available:** `akaunting` is **BUSL-1.1** (`akaunting/LICENSE.txt`,
> `composer.json` `"license": "BUSL-1.1"`) with an Additional Use Grant that caps production use at
> two users / one company / one thousand invoices and forbids rebranding and any "Accounting
> Service" offering — **facts only, and do not vendor any of it**. **AGPL-3.0:** `openbb`
> (`openbb/LICENSE` header: "All files in this repository are licensed under the GNU Affero
> General Public License v3.0"), `frappe-books` (`package.json` `"license": "AGPL-3.0-only"`), and
> **all five OCA repos** (`LICENSE` = AGPL-3 in each; per-module `__manifest__.py` is mixed —
> reconcile 16 AGPL-3 / 2 LGPL-3, bank-statement-import 16/2, financial-tools 37/4, invoicing 65/9,
> payment 21/3). **GPL-3.0:** `dolibarr` (`COPYING`). **GPL-2.0-only:** `beancount`
> (`pyproject.toml` `license = { text = "GPL-2.0-only" }`, `COPYING`) and `beanquery`
> (`license = 'GPL-2.0-only'`, `LICENSE`). **Permissive:** `fava` MIT, `taxhacker` MIT,
> `stripe-agent-toolkit` MIT (Stripe 2024–2025), `bank-mcp` MIT, `ai-books-mcp` MIT, `fingpt` MIT,
> `finrobot` Apache-2.0 (+ `NOTICE` and a `TRADEMARK_POLICY.md`). **No LICENSE file:**
> `plaid-mcp-server` (`package.json` says `"license": "MIT"`; the README is a **0-byte file**).
> Net: of the 19 wave-3 repos, **11 are copyleft or source-available** and are fact-sources only.

## 2. Agentic-benchmark methodology references

| Repo (dir) | URL | What it contains | Size | Why it matters to finance-world |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tau-bench` | https://github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench | Sierra's τ-bench (README marks it superseded by τ²). Domains retail (16 tools) + airline (14); DB is plain JSON reloaded per episode; each tool is a class with `invoke(data, **kwargs)` + `get_info()`; policy = `wiki.md` + `rules.py` as system prompt; `Task{user_id, instruction, actions, outputs}`; user simulator with `human\|llm\|react\|verify\|reflection` strategies ending on `###STOP###`. | 59 MB | The canonical recipe for **stateful write grading**: sha256 the post-episode DB, replay the gold actions on a fresh DB, compare hashes — **any incidental write fails**. Plus `pass^k`. Answers PLAN.md open question 4. MIT. |
| `tau2-bench` *(sparse)* | https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench | τ²/τ³: pydantic-typed framework, pluggable domains (`data_model.py` + `tools.py` with `@is_tool` + `environment.py` + `db.json` + `policy.md` + `tasks.json`), half- and full-duplex orchestrators. Domains: airline 50, retail 114, telecom 2,285, mock 10, **`banking_knowledge` 97**. Excluded: `data/tau2/results/` (604 MB of published runs), `data/voice/`, `telecom/tasks_voice.json`, `retail/task_issues/`, `web/`, `figs/`. | 60 MB | Two things we should copy. (1) **Composable reward**: `reward_basis` multiplies any subset of `{DB, ENV_ASSERTION, COMMUNICATE, NL_ASSERTION, ACTION}` — `COMMUNICATE` requires the agent to actually *tell the user* specific facts, which our submit-answer design only half-covers. (2) The `banking_knowledge` domain (below). MIT. |
| `TheAgentCompany` | https://github.com/TheAgentCompany/TheAgentCompany | CMU's simulated-software-company benchmark: **175 tasks** (verified: `workspaces/tasks/`), each a Docker image with `task.md` + `checkpoints.md` + `evaluator.py` + `scenarios.json` (NPC personas), over self-hosted GitLab/ownCloud/Plane/RocketChat. Category split: sde 69, hr 29, pm 28, admin 15, ds 14, **finance 12**, research/qa/ml 2 each. | 12 MB | The **checkpointed partial-credit** grading style, the multi-system fragmentation our `cross_system` family imitates, and — unexpectedly — a real finance task suite (`finance-apply-tax-credit`, `finance-budget-variance`, `finance-revenue-reconciliation`, `finance-check-attendance-payroll`, `finance-invoice-matching`, `finance-expense-validation`, `finance-find-signatories`, `finance-substantial-presence-test`, `finance-r-d-activities`, `finance-create-10k-income-report`, ±2 reimbursement tasks). MIT. |

## 3. Real tool surfaces (for 1:1 mock fidelity)

| Repo (dir) | URL | What it contains | Size | Why it matters to finance-world |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sec-edgar-mcp` | https://github.com/stefanoamorelli/sec-edgar-mcp | Python FastMCP over `edgartools`. **21 tools** in 5 groups: company (`get_cik_by_ticker`, `get_company_info`, `search_companies`, `get_company_facts`), filings (`get_recent_filings`, `get_filing_content`, `analyze_8k`, `get_filing_sections`), financial (`get_financials`, `get_segment_data`, `get_key_metrics`, `compare_periods`, `discover_company_metrics`, `get_xbrl_concepts`, `discover_xbrl_concepts`), insider/Form-4 (`get_insider_transactions`, `get_insider_summary`, `get_form4_details`, `analyze_form4_transactions`, `analyze_insider_sentiment`), `get_recommended_tools`. Paging = **char offset + budget** (`offset`, `max_chars=50000`) and `days`/`limit` windows. Errors return `{"success": false, "error": ...}`. | 1.5 MB | The reference our `filings_server.py` is shaped against. Two things to steal: the **`_FINANCIAL_INSTRUCTIONS` block embedded in every docstring** (use only returned data, never round, always cite the filing URL + date + form type), and the insider/Form-4 surface we lack entirely. **AGPL-3.0 — do not copy code.** |
| `financial-datasets-mcp-server` | https://github.com/financial-datasets/mcp-server | 376-line single-file FastMCP, **11 tools**: `get_income_statements`, `get_balance_sheets`, `get_cash_flow_statements`, `get_current_stock_price`, `get_historical_stock_prices`, `get_company_news`, `get_sec_filings`, + 4 crypto. No pagination, no structured errors. | 68 KB | Minimal contrast case for our XBRL-first `filings_server` — and a caution: its README documents 10 tools while the code has 11. MIT. |
| `ramp_mcp` | https://github.com/ramp-public/ramp_mcp | Ramp's official server, **19 tools max**. Distinctive design: it does **not** return API rows — it loads Ramp data into an in-memory SQLite DB and hands the model SQL (`load_transactions`, `load_receipts`, `load_reimbursements`, `load_bills`, `load_vendors`, `load_spend_limits`, `load_spend_programs`, `load_entities`, `load_users`, … then `process_data` / `execute_query` / `clear_table`). Loader tools **register only if the matching OAuth scope was granted**. Pagination auto-followed and hidden, capped at `CLIENT_MAX_PAGES=100` → forces better filters. Amounts are **integer minor units** ("1000 = $10.00"). | 116 KB | **Our biggest tool-surface gap**: `expense_audit` runs through sheets/docs with no real T&E system. | `modern-treasury-openapi` | https://github.com/Modern-Treasury/modern-treasury-openapi | The authoritative MT API spec: **177 operations** over payment_orders, expected_payments, returns, reversals, ledgers/ledger_accounts/ledger_transactions, balance monitors, counterparties, external/internal/virtual accounts, invoices, legal entities, holds, settlements. | 712 KB | The real vocabulary for **payment execution + bank matching**: `createExpectedPayment` vs `createTransaction` *is* the bank-rec problem, and `createReturn`/`createReversal` model ACH failures we don't simulate at all. |
| `erpnext-mcp-server` | https://github.com/rakeshgangwar/erpnext-mcp-server | The plain-vanilla **generic-CRUD-over-doctypes** wrapper for Frappe/ERPNext (TS, v0.1.0): `get_documents`, `get_document`, `create_document`, `update_document`, `submit_document`, `cancel_document`, `call_method`, `run_report`, `get_doctype_fields`, … ~12 tools total. Auth is an API key/secret header (`token <key>:<secret>`). Everything semantic lives in the *data* (DocType and field names), nothing in the tool signatures. | 200 KB | Access-pattern **class A** in the census: one `get/create/update/delete` pair parameterised by an entity-name string. Cheap to build, brutal to use — the model must know or discover the DocType vocabulary before it can do anything. It is the anti-pattern that justifies our `erp` mock's discovery-first shape. Also half of the **wire-format disagreement** below. MIT. |
| `erpnext-mcp-server-extended` | https://github.com/Kai-Oesterling/erpnext-mcp-server-extended | A fork of the above with ~19 tools, adding **schema mutation** (create DocTypes, Custom Fields, Property Setters, Workflows) plus `get_doctype_meta`, `get_workflow`/`create_workflow`/`update_workflow`, and an interactive `authenticate_erpnext` → `/api/method/login` path alongside key/secret. Maps Frappe's HTTP oddities: 417 = validation error, 409 = concurrent modification, 403 = permission. | 56 KB | Two exports. (1) **Two wrappers of one API that disagree on the wire**: create posts `{data: doc}` here vs a bare doc there, and submit posts the full document vs only `{doctype, name}` — one of each pair must fail against a live instance. That is a shipped, real instance of "the docs and the client disagree", not an invented chaos. (2) A **doubly-encoded error envelope** (`_server_messages` is a JSON array of JSON strings) and 417-not-400 for validation — the error-decoding task family in one repo. MIT. |

| Repo (dir) | URL | What it contains | Size | Why it matters to finance-world |

| `erpnext` *(sparse)* | https://github.com/frappe/erpnext | Full ERPNext source minus `erpnext/locale/` (107 MB of .po files). **192 doctypes under `accounts/`** and ~50 accounting reports, each doctype = JSON field schema + Python business logic + tests. Also `buying/` (purchase_order, supplier_scorecard) and `selling/` (customer_credit_limit, sales_order). | 43 MB | The single richest **open-source model of real AP/AR/GL mechanics** — field-level schemas and posting logic we can mine for realistic state and for task ideas (see §7). **GPL-3.0 — mine the schema, not the code.** |
| `d365-fasttrack-finance` *(sparse)* | https://github.com/microsoft/Dynamics-365-FastTrack-Implementation-Assets | Only `ERP/Finance/**` checked out (repo total is 751 MB). Content is thin: an **Invoice Capture** (OCR AP automation) guide incl. price-unit handling, and a customer-statement-printing optimization note. Excluded: a 96 MB installation-walkthrough MP4 and all non-Finance modules. | 2.1 MB | Marginal. Its one contribution is the **OCR invoice-capture → PO-match → price-unit mismatch** workflow, which is a real AP exception type. MIT. |
| `valuecell` | https://github.com/ValueCell-ai/valuecell | A shipping multi-agent *investment* platform (Python + frontend, Apache-2.0): a super-agent → Planner → per-agent task state machine, with `configs/agent_cards/*.json` advertising each agent's skills and example prompts. Agents: ResearchAgent (`fetch_periodic_sec_filings`, `fetch_event_sec_filings`, `fetch_ashare_filings`, `insert_md_file_to_knowledge`), NewsAgent, Planner (`tool_get_enabled_agents`, `tool_get_agent_description`), and a paper-trading runtime (`PaperTradingGateway.execute`, `BaseComposer._normalize_quantity/_normalize_plan/_apply_quantity_filters`, `TradeInstruction`/`PortfolioView`/`PositionSnapshot`). Streaming events: `tool_call_started`/`tool_call_completed`/`message_chunk`/`component_generator`/`done`/`failed`. | 12 MB | Not an eval — a **write-path architecture reference**. Its `proposal → deterministic normalizer → execution report` split is the general shape for any ERP write we ever grade (post a journal entry, create a collection letter, approve an invoice): the LLM proposes, deterministic Python normalizes and validates against constraints (`min_notional`, `max_positions`, `quantity_step`, `max_leverage`), and the report is what gets scored. Also two chaos primitives: **silent capability degradation** (when the embedder is unavailable the knowledge base becomes `None` and `search_knowledge` flips to `False` with only a log line — the agent keeps answering, degraded, and never says so), and a **market-scope hole** (US-exchange-only ticker lookup with A-shares behind a separate tool in a different identifier space). Apache-2.0. |
| `frappe-books` | https://github.com/frappe/books | Frappe Books v0.37.0, **AGPL-3.0-only**. A desktop (Electron + Vue) double-entry book-keeping app whose whole domain is **declarative JSON schemas**: `schemas/app/*.json` (~60 files — `Account`, `AccountingLedgerEntry`, `JournalEntry`/`JournalEntryAccount`, `Invoice`, `SalesInvoice`/`PurchaseInvoice` + `*Item` + `*ItemTax`, `Payment`/`PaymentFor`/`PaymentMethod`, `Party`, `Tax`/`TaxDetail`/`TaxSummary`, `PriceList`, `PricingRule`, `LoyaltyProgram`, `NumberSeries`, `POSProfile`, plus `inventory/`, `regional/`, `meta/`), each field carrying `fieldname / fieldtype / target / required / readOnly / section` — a Frappe DocType schema in miniature, without the Python. `models/` mirrors them in TS; `models/Transactional/LedgerPosting.ts` is the posting engine (`debit()`/`credit()` accumulate into `debitMap`/`creditMap`, `_validateIsEqual()` throws `ValidationError` on any imbalance, and a `roundOff` path books the residual to a round-off account). `reports/` ships `TrialBalance`, `BalanceSheet`, `ProfitAndLoss`, `GeneralLedger`, `GoodsAndServiceTax`, over a shared `AccountReport.ts`/`LedgerReport.ts`. `fyo/` is the mini-framework (`docHandler`, `dbHandler`, `authHandler`, `converter`). There is also an `ERPNextSyncSettings` / `ERPNextSyncQueue` / `FetchFromERPNextQueue` / `IntegrationErrorLog` cluster — a two-system sync with its own error log. | 5.9 MB | The **third Frappe-family schema source**, and the most readable one: `AccountingLedgerEntry` is 10 fields (`date, party, account, debit, credit, referenceType, referenceName, reverted, reverts`) versus ERPNext's 192 accounting doctypes, so it is the right size to copy a *shape* from rather than mine. Three concrete items: (1) `reverted` + `reverts` (a self-link) makes **reversal a ledger fact, not a deletion** — the exact primitive our `close_mgmt` accrual-reversal tasks need and that our ledger lacks; (2) `roundOff` as a *named posting account* for the residual is the honest answer to "the JE is off by a cent" and a good trap (an agent that plugs the difference into an expense account is wrong in a specific, checkable way); (3) `ERPNextSyncQueue` + `IntegrationErrorLog` is a shipped **queue-and-error-log** between two books systems — the missing middle of our `cross_system` family, which currently fragments data but never queues it. **AGPL-3.0 — mine the schemas, not the code.** |
| `akaunting` | https://github.com/akaunting/akaunting | Akaunting v3.1.15, Laravel. ⚠️ **BUSL-1.1, not open source** (see the licensing note). `routes/api.php` is 84 lines / **41 `Route::` declarations** over a small, very legible REST surface: `apiResource` for `users`, `companies`, `dashboards`, `items`, `contacts`, `documents`, `documents.transactions`, `accounts`, **`reconciliations`**, `transactions`, **`transfers`**, `categories`, `currencies`, `taxes`, `settings`, each with paired `{id}/enable` + `{id}/disable` GETs, plus `ping` and a `translations/{locale}/{file}` pair. Schema is 13 `core_v*` migrations declaring ~50 tables (`documents`/`document_items`/`document_item_taxes`/`document_totals`/`document_histories`, the legacy `invoices`/`bills` triples, `transactions`/`transaction_taxes`, `accounts`, `reconciliations`, `transfers`, `recurring`, `categories`, `currencies`, `taxes`, `roles`/`permissions`/`role_permissions`/`user_permissions`, `firewall_ips`/`firewall_logs`). `app/Models/Banking/Reconciliation.php` is the interesting one: fillable `['company_id','account_id','started_at','ended_at','closing_balance','transactions','reconciled','created_from','created_by']` with `'transactions' => 'array'` — **the whole reconciliation is one row with a JSON blob of transaction ids and a boolean**. | 58 MB | Modest value, and worth being blunt about it: most of the 58 MB is compiled frontend assets, and the API is generic Laravel `apiResource` CRUD with the business meaning entirely in the model layer. Two things justify keeping it. (1) It is the **only repo in the corpus that models a bank reconciliation as a first-class persisted object with an explicit period and a closing balance** (`started_at`/`ended_at`/`closing_balance`/`reconciled`) rather than as a per-line matching state — which is how a controller actually thinks about it, and a better fit for our `bank_rec` deliverable than line-by-line buckets. (2) The `documents` ↔ legacy `invoices`/`bills` duality is a shipped **schema-migration seam**: two generations of tables coexist, so "which table is the truth?" is a real question inside one system. **BUSL-1.1 — facts only, and nothing lifted.** |
| `taxhacker` | https://github.com/vas3k/taxhacker | MIT (Vasily Zubarev), v0.8.5, Next.js + Prisma/Postgres. A self-hosted **AI accountant for receipts/invoices**. 238-line `prisma/schema.prisma`, 13 models — the load-bearing four are `File` (`mimetype`, `metadata`, `isReviewed`, `isSplitted`, `cachedParseResult`), `Field` (**user-defined extraction fields**: `code`, `name`, `type`, `llm_prompt`, `options`, `isRequired`, `isExtra`, `isVisibleInList`, `isVisibleInAnalysis`), `Transaction` (`merchant`, `total`, `currencyCode`, `convertedTotal`, `convertedCurrencyCode`, `items Json`, `extra Json`, `categoryCode`, `projectCode`, `issuedAt`, `text`) and `Category`/`Project` (each with their own `llm_prompt`). `ai/schema.ts` is the mechanism: `fieldsToJsonSchema(fields)` builds a **structured-output JSON schema at runtime from the user's field rows** — every field with an `llm_prompt` becomes a property whose `description` *is* that prompt, then the same property set is nested under a required `items[]` array ("Separate items, products or transactions in the file… Find all items!"), with `additionalProperties: false` and everything `required`. `ai/prompt.ts` does template substitution of `{fields}`, `{categories}`, `{projects}`, `{categories.code}`, `{projects.code}` into a user-editable prompt. `ai/attachments.ts` caps analysis at `MAX_PAGES_TO_ANALYZE = 4`. Also an email-ingest app (IMAP presets) and an invoice generator under `app/(app)/apps/`. | 16 MB | The **document→structured-fields extraction pattern**, which is the front half of AP that finance-world starts *after*. Three transferable pieces. (1) **The extraction schema is data, not code** — categories and custom fields carry their own LLM prompts, so the same document yields different fields per tenant. That is a ready-made task variant axis (same invoice PDF, different chart of accounts / required fields) with no re-authoring. (2) `MAX_PAGES_TO_ANALYZE = 4` is a shipped, honest **truncation limit on document understanding** — a 9-page invoice is silently read as 4 pages. Our `docs_server` truncates by characters; page-capped OCR is the version that actually loses a total. (3) `convertedTotal`/`convertedCurrencyCode` alongside `total`/`currencyCode` on every row is the minimal **dual-currency carry** — and `total` is a plain `Int`, i.e. the minor-units trap again (cf. `ramp_mcp`). MIT — this one is a legal code source. |
| `finrobot` | https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinRobot | Apache-2.0 (+ `NOTICE`, `TRADEMARK_POLICY.md`). AutoGen-based multi-agent *investment research* platform. `finrobot/agents/agent_library.py` = a 10-role library (`Software_Developer`, `Data_Analyst`, `Programmer`, `Accountant`, `Statistician`, `IT_Specialist`, `Artificial_Intelligence_Engineer`, `Financial_Analyst`, `Market_Analyst`, `Expert_Investor`); `finrobot/toolkits.py` has one function, `register_toolkits(tools, caller, executor)`, that binds plain Python callables as AutoGen tools; `finrobot/data_source/` wraps FinnHub, FMP, yfinance, SEC, Reddit, and an `earnings_calls_src`/`filings_src`/`marker_sec_src` trio; `finrobot/functional/` is the tool bank (`analyzer.py` = `ReportAnalysisUtils`, plus `charting`, `quantitative`, `rag`, `ragquery`, `reportlab`, `coding`, `text`). `configs/save_config_forecaster.json` is a saved AutoGen "build" — five generated agents (financial_data_analyst, market_news_researcher, python_programmer, stock_price_estimator, financial_report_writer) each with a full system message ending in `"TERMINATE"`. 12 MB of the checkout is `report/` (three sample PDFs incl. a Microsoft 10-K and an NVDA report). | 25 MB | **Low-to-moderate value; keep for one idea, not for the domain.** The domain is equity research, which finance-world deliberately does not model. What is worth having is the `configs/*.json` artifact: an **agent roster generated from a one-paragraph task statement and then frozen to disk**, system messages and all — the clearest example in the corpus of role definitions as *data*. If we ever ship multi-persona tasks (an NPC controller with a stated remit), this is the file format to copy. Its cautionary half is equally useful: every generated persona is told to write and run Python for arithmetic, which is exactly the pattern `odoo-ai-agent` bans (pre-compute in Python, never let the LLM do the math) — two shipping systems, opposite rules, and only one of them is defensible for a graded number. Apache-2.0. |
| `fingpt` | https://github.com/AI4Finance-Foundation/FinGPT | MIT, same foundation as `finrobot`. Predominantly **LLM training code, not an agent surface**: `fingpt/FinGPT_Benchmark` (LoRA instruction-tuning over financial NLP tasks — sentiment, headline classification, NER, relation extraction; `data/download.py` pulls from HuggingFace, so **no dataset is in the checkout**), `FinGPT_Sentiment_Analysis_v1/v3`, `FinGPT_RAG`, `FinGPT_MultiAgentsRAG`, `FinGPT_Forecaster`, `FinGPT_FinancialReportAnalysis`, `FinGPT_ForexIntelligence`, `FinGPT_Others/{FinGPT_Trading, FinGPT_Robo_Advisor, FinGPT_Low_Code_Development}`, plus four training notebooks at the root. 7 MB is `figs/`. The one non-training subtree is `finogrid/` (616 KB) — a B2B stablecoin payout / agent-to-agent micropayment platform with `corridors/{argentina, brazil, india, indonesia, nigeria, philippines, uae, vietnam}/adapter.py`, four agents (`treasury_strategy`, `audit_governance`, `ops_oversight`, `internal_support`, `process_improvement`) and six `mcp/*/server.py` files (`plaid`, `bridge`, `identity`, `kyt_aml`, `kya_validator`, `wallet_factory`, 1,091 lines total) — which despite the `mcp/` path are **FastAPI request/response services, not MCP servers** (`async def create_link_token(request: CreateLinkTokenRequest)` etc., no tool registration anywhere). | 24 MB | **Low value — keep for completeness, and record why.** It is a fine-tuning repo for financial *NLP classification*, an axis finance-world does not grade; the benchmark data is not in the tree; and its one agentic subproject is crypto-payout infrastructure whose "MCP servers" are misnamed REST services. The single honest export is negative and worth writing down: `finogrid/mcp/` is the corpus's clearest instance of **MCP-as-a-label** — a directory named `mcp` containing no MCP whatsoever — which is a real hazard when auto-surveying repos for tool surfaces, and the reason every count in this index is taken from registration sites in code rather than from paths or READMEs. MIT. |

## 5. The ERP-vendor axis

Wave 2's organising idea: finance-world models exactly one ERP (D365-shaped) and has no evidence
about how *other* vendors' systems behave. These repos supply one system per vendor — the schema,
the driving surface, or both — so that "what does an ERP look like from an agent's seat?" stops
being a D365-only answer.

| Repo (dir) | URL | What it contains | Size | Why it matters to finance-world |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `odoo` *(sparse)* | https://github.com/odoo/odoo | **Odoo 19.0 final** (`odoo/release.py`, `version_info = (19, 0, 0, FINAL, 0, '')`). Sparse: `addons/{account, purchase, sale, payment, analytic}` + `odoo/addons/base` + a handful of core files (`http.py`, `exceptions.py`, `sql_db.py`). `account` and `purchase` are LGPL-3 per their manifests. The whole AP/AR model: `account_move` (polymorphic, 7 `move_type` values), `account_move_line`, `account_partial_reconcile`, `account_full_reconcile`, `account_payment_term(_line)`, `account_bank_statement_line`, `account_reconcile_model`, `purchase_order(_line)`, plus two read-only SQL views (`purchase.bill.line.match`, `purchase.bill.union`). | 205 MB | The **second ERP data model**, and it is structurally opposite to ours: no AR/AP subledger split, one polymorphic `account_move` discriminated by `move_type` (the NetSuite pattern) versus D365's `CustTrans`/`VendTrans` split. Three shippable traps come straight out of the source: (1) **the header due date lies** — an invoice is split into one open item per payment-term installment, each with its own `date_maturity`, while `invoice_date_due` is only `max(date_maturity)`; (2) **selection values that never occur** — `payment_state` advertises `in_payment` and `invoicing_legacy`, which community code cannot produce; (3) **the three-way-match rule is per line**, decided by a per-product `purchase_method` (ordered vs received), so a service line billed on ordered quantity must not raise a false exception. 153 MB of the checkout is `i18n/*.po` — the prune candidate. **LGPL-3 — mine the schema, not the code.** |
| `odoo-ai-agent` | https://theodooagent.com (frontend repo; the LangGraph backend is a separate **private** repo) | The Next.js frontend of a shipping production Odoo agent, plus `documents/BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE.md` — a detailed public description of the LangGraph StateGraph behind it. Odoo verbs the agent drives over XML-RPC: `search_count`, `search_read`, `read_group`, `create`, `write`, `action_confirm`/`action_cancel` via method call, `ir.actions.report`. Its own API: `POST /chat/{id}/stream` (SSE), `/action`, `/upload`, `/search`, `GET /chat/{id}/audit`, `/notifications`, `POST /test-connection`, `POST /chat/{id}/pin/{pinId}/refresh`. | 2.5 MB | The **write-and-approve protocol**, sourced from something that actually ships. Every write passes an explicit confirmation gate: `action_proposal {action, model, vals, target_ids, method, status:'pending_confirmation'}` → `POST /chat/{id}/action` → typed result, with **422 reserved for Odoo *business* errors carrying per-field detail** (distinct from 400 validation). Two more transferable rules: the LLM never does arithmetic (a Data Formatter node pre-computes every total in Python and hands exact values to the model, and when results are paginated the executor fetches global totals separately via `read_group` so a page subtotal cannot be mistaken for the dataset total); and ambiguity resolution needs **ten distinct prompt shapes**, not one. Chaos: `odoo_was_truncated` + `odoo_total_count` self-reporting reads, a 45 s read cache creating a read-after-write staleness window, and pinned dashboard tiles frozen until an explicit refresh. **No LICENSE file** — facts only. |
| `sap-fiori-browser-automation` | https://github.com/Browser-Automation-Hub/sap-fiori-browser-automation | Playwright/Anchor-browser automation for SAP Fiori, MIT. **3 of its 5 advertised actions are real** (`login_fiori`, `create_purchase_order`, `approve_workflow`); `extract_financial_data` and `manage_invoices` are TODO stubs. The real content is the step sequences and the shared machinery: an `ActionBuilder` DSL (`.login/.navigate/.waitForSelector/.click/.type/.extractTable/.extractText/.screenshot/.waitDelay/.do/.run`), `createSession`/`loadSession`/`saveSession`, `retry`/`humanDelay`/`waitForNetworkIdle`/`safeEvaluate`, and typed errors (`AuthenticationError`, `SelectorNotFoundError`, `SessionExpiredError`, `RateLimitError`) that are **defined but never thrown**. | 72 KB | The only repo in the corpus that documents a **real multi-step ERP UI walk**: SAP Fiori login alone is a 9-step sequence with three different timeouts (20 s username, 15 s password, 30 s post-login shell), a conditional MFA branch, and an error screenshot — *before* any business work starts. finance-world's walks currently begin at step 10. Two structural hazards it makes concrete: write actions are wrapped in `retry({attempts:3, delay:2000, backoff:1.5})` **and** each `.click()` retries at `{attempts:2}`, so a timeout after a server-side commit produces a duplicate approval/post; and three `waitForSelector(...).catch(()=>{})` sites mean optional popups that may or may not appear and must not hang the flow. |
| `oracle-ebs-browser-automation` | https://github.com/Browser-Automation-Hub/oracle-ebs-browser-automation | Same author/template, MIT. **0 of 5 advertised actions implemented** — `login_ebs`, `navigate_responsibility`, `submit_requisition`, `approve_po`, `run_concurrent_request` are all the identical TODO stub returning `{status:'ok', data:null}`. README says "Selector reference not yet documented". `src/{utils,session,custom-actions}.js` are line-for-line identical to the SAP repo's (111/95/150 lines); `auth.js` (314 lines) differs only in comments and default BASE_URL. | 72 KB | Value is entirely in the **vocabulary and the fraud**. The vocabulary: `navigate_responsibility` and `run_concurrent_request` name two Oracle EBS concepts finance-world has no analogue for — role/responsibility context (data invisible under the wrong responsibility, so an empty result is a permission artifact, not a zero) and submit-poll-retrieve batch jobs. The fraud: a success-shaped envelope over no work done, which combined with the SAP and Sage repos gives **12 of 15 shipped ERP actions returning `{status:'ok', data:null}`** — the wave's single most portable new chaos primitive. |
| `sage-300-browser-automation` | https://github.com/Browser-Automation-Hub/sage-300-browser-automation | Same template, MIT. **0 of 5 implemented**: `login_sage`, `create_journal_entry`, `process_ap_invoice`, `run_financial_report`, `update_inventory`. Shared machinery byte-identical to the other two. | 72 KB | Names the three SMB-ERP write verbs our world does not model at all — author-and-post a balanced journal entry, key an AP invoice, run a parameterised financial report over a `DateFrom`/`DateTo` window and answer from the export. With Oracle EBS it defines the **`journal_entry` / `ap_invoice_entry` / `batch_job_ops` / `role_context`** gap families in `research/erp-workflow-automation.md`. |

**Vendor coverage after wave 2** (which vendor is grounded by what kind of source):

| Vendor | Data model / schema | Agent-facing tool surface | UI / step sequences | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Microsoft D365 Finance | `erp-domain.md` + `microsoft-FinanceBenchmark` extracts | dynamic ERP MCP (discovery → query → action) | — | **Modelled.** The world's primary ERP. |
| Odoo | `odoo` (LGPL, full `account`/`purchase`) | `odoo-ai-agent` (XML-RPC verbs + confirm gate); `mcp-erp-multivendor/src/odoo.rs` | `erp-bench` `tasks_ui/` (browser modality) | **Best-documented alternative.** Blocked on Q18. |
| ERPNext / Frappe | `erpnext` (192 accounting doctypes) | `erpnext-mcp-server` + `-extended` (two disagreeing wrappers) | — | Schema maps 1:1 onto our three-layer model. |

| SAP | — | `sap-erp-mcp-cdata` (3 SQL tools) | `sap-fiori-browser-automation` (3 real actions) | Thinnest schema coverage in the set. |
| Oracle EBS | — | — | `oracle-ebs-browser-automation` (all stubs) | **Vocabulary only.** Names the concepts; verifies nothing. |
| Sage 300 | — | — | `sage-300-browser-automation` (all stubs) | Vocabulary only. |
| ECOUNT | `mcp-server-ecount/docs/*.md` (11 API analyses) | `mcp-server-ecount` (23 tools) | — | Source of the tiered-rate-limit friction template. |

## 7. What these add that finance-world doesn't cover yet

Cross-referenced against the 15 task dirs in `tasks/`, the 7 servers in `mcp/servers/`, and
§5 of `research/evals-and-benchmarks.md`. Only genuinely *new* items are listed.

**New eval task types**

1. **Scale/unit as a graded field** (TAT-QA). 5,543 arithmetic questions each carry a required
   `scale` label; a right number with the wrong magnitude scores zero. Our verifiers compare
   values, not units — a one-line probe addition with real discriminative power.
2. **Tool-plan grading, incl. expected parallel calls** (FinMCP-Bench). Grade the *sequence* of
   tool calls against a gold plan (precision/recall/F1) rather than only the final state, with
   `para_tool_call_number` as an explicit difficulty axis. Our oracle walks already encode the
   gold plan — this is nearly free signal about *how* the agent got there.
3. **Refusal as a first-class label** (financebench `results/`). Its 16 run files score
   Correct / Incorrect / **Refusal** separately. We have empty-answer traps but score them
   binary; splitting "wrongly refused" from "wrongly answered" would sharpen the too_hard call.
4. **Multi-month drift** (accounting-bench `multi-month-close`). One task, three sequential
   months, where month 2's errors compound into month 3 — deferred revenue on annual contracts,
   a December bonus accrual that must be *reversed*, and AWS prepaid capitalization with monthly
   amortization. Our `close_mgmt` is single-period.
5. **Multi-document reconciliation with inconsistency codes** (FinBalance, paper-only but
   reproducible): from a bundle of OCR'd source docs — deliberately mixed *posting*, *support*,
   and **distractor** documents — emit **cited** journal entries, a balance sheet, and a code
   from a fixed taxonomy for each inconsistency found. Grading via **BS_recon** (replay the
   statements back through a ledger) is the strongest anti-plug-entry design published, and it
   answers the reward-hacking failure mode AccountingBench documents.
6. **Conversational decomposition with cross-turn references** (ConvFinQA). 11,104 turns where
   turn *n*'s program references turn *n−1*'s *result* (`#0`). Our multi-turn `session` support
   exists but no task currently requires carrying a computed value across turns.

**New workflow scenarios (mostly from ERPNext's 192 accounting doctypes + the MT spec)**

7. **Payment reconciliation / un-reconciliation** (`payment_reconciliation`,
   `process_payment_reconciliation`, `unreconcile_payment`): match unapplied payments and
   customer advances against open invoices with a partial-allocation queue — and, harder,
   *undo* a mis-application and re-apply it. Our `cash_app` applies cash; it never corrects it.
8. **Withholding tax with thresholds** (`tax_withholding_category` → `tax_deduction_basis`,
   `cumulative_threshold`, `transaction_threshold`, `tax_on_excess_amount`): compute 1099/TDS
   withholding on a vendor payment where the rate applies only to the excess over a
   *cumulative year-to-date* threshold. Pure arithmetic on ledger state — exactly verifiable.
9. **Dunning with interest and fees** (`dunning`: `rate_of_interest`, `dunning_fee`,
   `total_interest`, `overdue_payments` child table): our `collections_ops` escalates a letter
   *level*; ERPNext computes the interest and fee that go on the dunning notice.
10. **FX revaluation at period end** (`exchange_rate_revaluation` → `make_jv_entries`,
    unrealized gain/loss account, `pegged_currencies`): revalue open foreign-currency AR/AP and
    post the unrealized gain/loss JE. We have multi-currency data and no revaluation task.
11. **Period close and lock** (`accounting_period`, `period_closing_voucher`,
    `repost_accounting_ledger`): attempt a backdated posting into a closed period, then either
    refuse correctly or reopen/repost. A clean "does the agent respect controls?" probe.
12. **Rule-based bank auto-match + internal transfers** (`bank_transaction_rule`,
    `auto_reconcile_vouchers`, `create_internal_transfer`, `search_for_transfer_transaction`,
    report `cheques_and_deposits_incorrectly_cleared`): our `bank_rec` classifies into four
    buckets; the real trap is a **transfer between two of the company's own bank accounts**
    appearing as an unmatched debit *and* credit, which a naive agent books twice.
13. **ACH returns and payment reversals** (MT `createReturn`, `createReversal`,
    `createExpectedPayment`): a payment that settles, then bounces back days later (R01
    insufficient funds), must be un-applied and the invoice re-opened. Nothing in the world
    currently models a payment *failing after the fact*.
14. **Deferred revenue / prepaid amortization schedules** (`process_deferred_accounting`,
    `deferred_revenue_and_expense`, `subscription`): recognize one month of a 12-month contract.
15. **Supplier scorecard** (`supplier_scorecard` + criteria/period/variables): score a vendor
    from delivery and invoice-accuracy history — a natural escalation of `vendor_master`.
16. **Statement-of-account run** (`process_statement_of_accounts`, `psoa_*`): generate and send
    per-customer statements for a filtered set — a bulk, multi-entity write task.
17. **Ledger integrity bisect** (`bisect_accounting_statements`, `ledger_health_monitor`,
    report `invalid_ledger_entries`): given "the trial balance stopped balancing sometime this
    quarter", *find the date and the entry*. A genuinely agentic search task with an exact answer.
18. **OCR invoice capture → PO match with unit mismatch** (D365 FastTrack): the vendor invoices
    per-case while the PO is per-each; the price-unit mismatch is the exception. A concrete
    third exception type for the parked `threeway_match` family.

**New scenarios from TheAgentCompany's `finance/` suite** (12 tasks, none previously mined)

19. **Ask a colleague for a blocking input.** In `finance-apply-tax-credit` and
    `finance-find-signatories` the agent *must* message an NPC (finance director / sales
    director) on chat to get a folder path or resolve an ambiguity — the information exists
    nowhere else. Our world's `email_server` is read-only, so no task can require obtaining a
    missing fact from a person. This is the largest structural gap the survey found.
20. **Fill a real regulatory form.** `finance-apply-tax-credit`: complete **IRS Form 6765
    Section B (Alternative Simplified Credit)** from a wages CSV + a financials CSV, consulting
    the instructions PDF, and save the filled PDF. A form-filling deliverable, not a text answer.
21. **Budget-vs-actual variance with a compound flag rule.** `finance-budget-variance`: flag a
    department/category/month only when the variance exceeds **both 10% and $5,000**, after a
    seasonality adjustment; deliver the flagged keys as `Department_Category_YYYYMM`. Pairs with
    ERPNext's `budget_variance_report` / `monthly_distribution` (seasonal budget spreading).
22. **Signatory / delegation-of-authority extraction.** `finance-find-signatories`: pull
    name/title/company/date of every signature out of filing PDFs into a CSV, then report the
    count back to a named person. Authority-matrix questions ("who can approve this?") are a
    natural fit for our `pbc` and `payment_proposal` families.
23. **Payroll ↔ attendance reconciliation** (`finance-check-attendance-payroll`) and
    **expense-policy qualification** (`finance-expense-validation`, qualified vs non-qualified
    reimbursement) — a payroll subledger and a policy-driven expense decision, neither modelled.

**New environment / grading mechanics**

24. **Knowledge-retrieval as a difficulty axis** (τ² `banking_knowledge`): 97 tasks share a
    **698-document knowledge base**, and `--retrieval-config` swaps the agent's access to it —
    `no_knowledge`, `full_kb` (everything in context), `golden_retrieval`, `grep_only`, `bm25`,
    `openai_embeddings`, `qwen_embeddings`, `terminal_use` (a real shell), `alltools` — with
    `_reranker` and `_grep` suffixes composing. Same task, seven difficulty settings, no
    re-authoring. Our `docs_server` holds SOPs and policies and exposes exactly one retrieval
    mode; this is the cheapest available lever for growing tasks that came back `too_easy`.
25. **Discoverable / unlockable tools** (τ² `banking_knowledge`:
    `list_discoverable_agent_tools`, `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool`,
    `call_discoverable_agent_tool`, `give_discoverable_user_tool`): the tool surface is not
    fixed at t=0 — capabilities are revealed or handed over mid-conversation. A clean way to
    force genuine exploration instead of a memorized walk.
26. **Composable reward bases** (τ² `reward_basis`): the score is the *product* of any subset of
    DB-equality, environment assertions, communicated-info checks, NL assertions, and
    action-trajectory matching; unlisted components still run as diagnostics. That last part is
    exactly what we want for flake triage — measure more than you grade.
27. **Permission variants as difficulty** (Ramp scope-gating, QuickBooks
    `DISABLE_WRITE/UPDATE/DELETE` by name prefix, Grafana `--disable-write`): ship the same task
    against a read-only vs read-write tool surface and see whether the agent finds the legal
    path. All three production servers do this; our `erp_server` has role filtering but no
    task-level variant that exercises it.
28. **SQL-over-loaded-data as a tool idiom** (Ramp): load once into SQLite, then let the model
    query. Combined with Ramp's **integer minor units** convention ("1000 = $10.00"), this is a
    realistic and nasty precision trap — a correct SQL aggregate reported 100× too large.
29. **Contamination-resistant graders** (TheAgentCompany): evaluators ship **Fernet-encrypted**
    (`evaluator.py.enc`, key via env) so a browsing agent can't read its own rubric. Worth
    considering before any public release of finance-world tasks.

**Tool-surface gaps worth closing**

- No **T&E / corporate-card** system (`ramp_mcp`) despite an `expense_audit` family.
- No **payment-rails / bank** surface (`modern-treasury-openapi`) — payments are executed
  inside the ERP mock, so returns, reversals and expected-payment matching are unreachable.
- No **second books dialect** (`xero-mcp-server`) for the subsidiary fragmentation story.

**Wave-2 additions (2026-08-11)** — continuing the numbering; only items not already above.

30. **One shared template context as the anti-drift mechanism** (`erp-bench`). Instruction,
    verifier, oracle and seed data are all rendered from a single solved Python object, so the
    verifier's expected numbers and the oracle's plan cannot disagree. Our exporter renders the
    same four artifacts from separate code paths. This is the cheapest structural fix in the wave.
31. **Objective non-collapse as a ship gate** (`erp-bench`). A task is rejected unless optimizing
    the stated objective produces a *different* answer than the naive cost minimizer — verified by
    re-solving with the naive objective pinned. Stronger than measuring `too_easy` after the fact.
32. **Unsatisfiable demand as a first-class tag** (`erp-bench`, 77 of 300 tasks). The correct
    answer necessarily includes rejections, and the generator refuses to ship the scenario unless
    it contains both kept and rejected items. Our empty-answer traps test "no data"; this tests
    "the data says no".
33. **The lying tool** (`sap-fiori` / `oracle-ebs` / `sage-300`). 12 of 15 shipped ERP actions
    return `{status:'ok', data:null}`. An agent that checks `status === 'ok'` and moves on is
    wrong, and nothing in our world currently punishes that.
34. **The propose → confirm → execute protocol** (`odoo-ai-agent`, `valuecell`). Every write in
    both shipping systems passes an explicit confirmation gate, with 422 reserved for *business*
    errors carrying per-field detail. Modelling it as a real two-turn protocol (proposal event,
    then a separate confirm call) is the only version that can catch an unconfirmed write.
35. **Retry-induced duplicate writes as a structural hazard** (browser trio). Whole write actions
    are wrapped in `retry({attempts:3})` and the step DSL retries each click at `{attempts:2}`, so
    a timeout after a server-side commit double-posts. Not probabilistic — structural, and
    therefore testable without a friction-rate source we don't have.
36. **Tiered per-API rate limits that force read planning** (`mcp-server-ecount`). 1 s single-read
    / 10 s write / **10 min bulk-read**, file-shared across processes. The only enforced rate-limit
    design in the corpus, and the cleanest way to make "choose one bulk call over a 40-call loop"
    a graded skill.
37. **Documentation drift as shipped reality**, now with four independent instances
    (`mcp-erp-multivendor` 79 code / 44 README / 34 manifest; `mcp-server-ecount` 22 logged vs 23
    registered; `sap-erp-mcp-cdata` README promising writes on a read-only server;
    `quickbooks-online-mcp-server` 142 files vs a 145 badge). Enough independent sourcing to ship
    "the tool roster you are told about is not the roster you have" as a deliberate chaos axis.

**Wave-3 additions (2026-08-11)** — continuing the numbering; only items not already above.

38. **A deterministic, executable query language over a ledger** (`beancount` + `beanquery`). BQL
    is a real grammar (`beanquery/parser/bql.ebnf`, 401 lines) with `SELECT … FROM … WHERE …
    GROUP BY … HAVING … ORDER BY … PIVOT BY … LIMIT`, a ledger-specific `FROM OPEN ON <date>
    CLOSE ON <date> CLEAR` clause, and 10 named tables. Every one of our numeric ground truths is
    currently produced by bespoke Python. A BQL-shaped read surface would make "what is the
    answer?" and "how would a controller get it?" the same artifact — and, unlike SQL-over-loaded-
    rows (`ramp_mcp`), it is *typed to accounting* (`cost()`, `value()`, `convert()`, `units()`,
    `getprice()`), so unit errors surface as type errors instead of wrong numbers.
39. **`PIVOT BY` and `CLEAR` as first-class query verbs** (`beanquery`). `CLEAR` closes income and
    expense into equity *as part of the query*, i.e. the closing entries are a read-time operation.
    That is the cleanest possible statement of the thing our `close_mgmt` tasks are really testing,
    and a good discriminator: an agent that reports a balance sheet without clearing is off by net
    income, an amount that is checkable to the cent.
40. **The `Pad` / `Balance` assertion pair** (`beancount/core/data.py` — `ALL_DIRECTIVES` is
    `Open, Close, Commodity, Pad, Balance, Transaction, Note, Event, Query, Price, Document,
    Custom`). A `Balance` directive is an **assertion checked by the engine at a date**, and `Pad`
    is the explicit, auditable plug that makes it true. finance-world has ties-out checks in
    verifiers but no in-world way for the *agent* to assert a balance and be told it fails — which
    is the single most common real control in a close.
41. **Booking-method ambiguity as a graded decision** (`beancount/core/data.py` `class Booking`:
    `STRICT`, `STRICT_WITH_SIZE`, `NONE`, `AVERAGE`, `FIFO`, `LIFO`, `HIFO`). A lot-matching
    choice that changes the number, is declared per-account, and errors loudly when ambiguous.
    Nothing in our world requires the agent to notice that the answer depends on a policy.
42. **A rule engine for bank matching, with the rules as data** (`oca-account-reconcile`
    `account_reconcile_model_oca`). `rule_type ∈ {invoice_matching, writeoff_suggestion,
    writeoff_button}`; candidate filtering by `match_nature` (amount_received / amount_paid),
    `match_amount` (lower / greater / between + min/max), `match_journal_ids`, `match_partner` +
    `match_partner_ids` + `match_partner_category_ids`, and text rules (`match_label`,
    `match_note`, `match_transaction_type` with `contains` / `not_contains` / `match_regex`
    params); and an `auto_reconcile` boolean meaning "this match is significant enough to post
    without a human". Our `bank_rec` asks the model to classify lines; this makes **authoring the
    rule** the task, which is both harder and exactly what a treasury analyst actually does.
43. **The bank feed as a scheduled, deduplicated pull** (`oca-bank-statement-import`
    `account_statement_import_online`). The provider object carries `interval_type` /
    `interval_number` / `update_schedule` / `next_run` / `last_successful_run` and a
    `statement_creation_mode ∈ {daily, weekly, monthly}`, and every imported line is deduped on
    **`unique_import_id`** before insert. Two task shapes fall straight out: a re-run that must not
    double-import (idempotency), and a gap between `last_successful_run` and today that the agent
    must notice before trusting a balance. Our fixtures are static files with neither.
44. **Format-level statement parsing as the actual first step** (`oca-bank-statement-import`:
    dedicated modules for **CAMT.053**, **CAMT.054**, **OFX** (+ an `ofx_by_acctid` variant),
    and spreadsheet/CSV/HTML imports with a configurable column map, all with committed test
    fixtures under `tests/`). Our `bank_rec` starts from a clean normalized table; the real job
    starts from a bank-specific file whose credit/debit sign convention and date semantics
    (booking vs value date) have to be established first.
45. **Journal/period locking as a distinct control from period close**
    (`oca-account-financial-tools`: `account_journal_lock_date`, `account_lock_date_update`,
    `account_lock_to_date`, `account_fiscal_year`, `account_move_name_sequence`,
    `account_invoice_constraint_chronology`, `account_journal_restrict_mode`,
    `account_move_template`, `account_netting`). §7.11 wanted "attempt a backdated posting into a
    closed period"; this repo names **five different locks** that can each refuse it for a
    different reason, plus a chronology constraint (invoice numbers must not go backwards in
    time) — which turns one probe into a diagnosis task: *which* control blocked the posting?
46. **Per-session tool activation, in production** (`openbb` `extensions/mcp_server`). See §3.
    Upgrades §7.25 from "a benchmark does this" to "a shipping platform does this", with a
    working design for the catalogue (`CategoryIndex`), the four admin tools, and schema
    compression to keep the visible surface cheap.
47. **A vendor benchmark laid out exactly like a Harbor task** (`stripe-agent-toolkit/benchmarks`).
    `environment/` + hidden `grader/` + hidden `solution/` + Dockerfile, best-of-3 scoring, infra
    failures discarded, winning transcript human-reviewed, and **224 published runs with turn
    counts**. Independent corroboration of our own task layout, and the only external turn-count
    distribution we can calibrate step budgets against.
48. **Extraction fields as tenant data** (`taxhacker` `ai/schema.ts` + `ai/prompt.ts`). The
    structured-output JSON schema is *generated at request time* from user-defined `Field` rows
    whose `llm_prompt` becomes the property description. Same document, different required fields
    per company — a task-variant axis that costs one fixture edit instead of a re-authoring.
49. **Reversal as a ledger fact** (`frappe-books` `AccountingLedgerEntry.reverted` +
    `reverts` self-link; `ai-books-mcp` `void_journal_entry(entry_id, reason, actor)`). Two
    independent systems model "undo" as a *new, linked, reasoned* record and never as an edit.
    Our ledger has no reversal primitive, which is why §7.4's multi-month accrual-reversal ladder
    has nowhere to land.
50. **The read-cache staleness ladder** (`bank-mcp` `src/utils/cache.ts`: balances 5 min /
    transactions 15 min / accounts 1 hr). Different TTLs over one dataset guarantee a
    self-inconsistent read. Sharper than `odoo-ai-agent`'s single 45 s cache because the
    inconsistency is *between two tools*, which is where an agent is least likely to look.

---

## 8. The double-entry engine + bank-reconciliation axis

Wave 3's organising idea, and the direct complement to wave 2's. Wave 2 asked "what does an ERP
look like from an agent's seat?" across vendors. Wave 3 asks the two questions underneath it:
**what is the smallest complete, deterministic accounting engine we could hold a task against**,
and **what does bank reconciliation actually look like in production code** — because `bank_rec`
and `cash_app` are two of our largest families and both were grounded, until now, only in D365
shapes plus the Odoo core model. The `beancount` triple answers the first (a plain-text ledger, a
real query language over it, and a web/JSON API in front of it). The five OCA repos answer the
second: they are Odoo **18.0** community addon suites — note the version skew against our
`odoo` clone, which is **19.0 FINAL**, so field names should be checked against `odoo/` before
being treated as current.

| Repo (dir) | URL | What it contains | Size | Why it matters to finance-world |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `beancount` | https://github.com/beancount/beancount | Martin Blais's plain-text double-entry engine, **GPL-2.0-only** (`COPYING`). `beancount/core/` is the model: `data.py` defines `ALL_DIRECTIVES = (Open, Close, Commodity, Pad, Balance, Transaction, Note, Event, Query, Price, Document, Custom)`, `Posting`/`Transaction` NamedTuples, and `class Booking(enum.Enum)` = `STRICT, STRICT_WITH_SIZE, NONE, AVERAGE, FIFO, LIFO, HIFO`; alongside `inventory.py`, `position.py`, `realization.py`, `interpolate.py`, `prices.py`, `number.py`, `display_context.py`. `beancount/parser/` is a real lexer+grammar (`lexer.l`, `grammar.y`, a C `decimal.c`) plus `booking.py`/`booking_full.py`. `beancount/ops/` = `balance.py`, `pad.py`, `summarize.py`, `validation.py`, `compress.py`, `lifetimes.py`, `documents.py`. 19 `plugins/` are pluggable ledger *assertions* (`check_commodity`, `check_closing`, `check_drained`, `check_average_cost`, `coherent_cost`, `leafonly`, `noduplicates`, `nounused`, `onecommodity`, `unique_prices`, `sellgains`, `pedantic`, `currency_accounts`, `implicit_prices`, `auto_accounts`, `close_tree`, `commodity_attr`, …). CLI: `bean-check`, `bean-doctor`, `bean-example`, `bean-format`, `treeify`. **Data**: `examples/example.beancount` is a **347 KB generated ledger**, plus `examples/simple/{basic,starter}.beancount` (643 / 371 lines), `examples/vesting/vesting.beancount`, and `examples/tutorial/` = ~25 **committed golden outputs** (`balances.output`, `balsheet.output`, `journal.output` (36 KB), `journal-unrestricted.output` (796 KB), `holdings*.output`, `networth.output`, `stats-*.output`). Nearly every module has a paired `*_test.py`. | 5.4 MB | The **deterministic accounting core** the corpus otherwise lacks: everything else here is an application over a database, this is the arithmetic with a formal grammar and an executable checker. Four things to take. (1) **`Balance` as an in-world assertion and `Pad` as the auditable plug** (§7.40) — the one control primitive our world has no agent-facing version of. (2) **Booking method as a policy that changes the number** (§7.41). (3) `bean-example`: a *generator* that emits a full realistic multi-year ledger, i.e. an existing answer to "where does plausible ledger seed data come from" that does not require inventing one. (4) `examples/tutorial/*.output` are **committed golden files for a text report** — the pattern for regression-testing our own report deliverables. **GPL-2.0 — mine the model and the vocabulary, not the code.** |
| `beanquery` | https://github.com/beancount/beanquery | The BQL engine, split out of beancount, **GPL-2.0-only**, `version = '0.3.0.dev0'`. `parser/bql.ebnf` (401 lines) is the full grammar: statements are `select | balances | journal | print | create_table | insert`; `SELECT [DISTINCT] targets [FROM …] [WHERE] [GROUP BY … HAVING …] [ORDER BY …] [PIVOT BY a, b] [LIMIT n]`, and the ledger-specific `FROM` clause is `OPEN ON <date> [CLOSE [ON <date>]] [CLEAR]` — period bounds and **closing-entries-into-equity as query syntax**. `sources/beancount.py` registers **10 tables** — `entries`, `postings` (the default when no table is named), `transactions`, `prices`, `balances`, `notes`, `events`, `documents`, `accounts`, `commodities` — with columns derived from the NamedTuple annotations, plus `position`/`cost`/`amount`/`transaction`/`open`/`close` sub-column types. `query_env.py` carries **103 `@function` registrations** (type-dispatched overloads over ~80 distinct names: `cost`, `value`, `convert`, `units`, `getprice`, `filter_currency`, `number`, `neg`, `abs`, `safediv`, `round`, `date`, `date_add`/`date_diff`/`date_trunc`/`date_bin`/`date_part`, `year`/`quarter`/`month`/`day`/`weekday`, `today`, `parent`/`root`/`leaf`/`has_account`/`account_sortkey`, `open_date`/`close_date`/`open_meta`/`entry_meta`/`any_meta`/`meta`, `grep`/`grepn`/`subst`/`substr`/`splitcomp`/`joinstr`/`upper`/`lower`/`length`/`maxwidth`, `possign`, …) and **11 `EvalAggregator` classes** (`count`, `sum` over int/Decimal/Amount/Position/Inventory, `first`, `last`, `min`, `max`). `sources/{csv,memory}.py` mean **non-ledger tables can be attached and joined**; `cursor.py` is a DB-API-ish surface; `shell.py` adds `.tables`, `.describe`, `.explain`, `.errors`, `.run`, `.format`, `.output`. Renderers: text, csv, beancount. | 580 KB | **The single most reusable artifact in wave 3.** It is a small, complete, *accounting-typed* query language with a published grammar, which is exactly the shape of a high-fidelity read tool that grades itself: the gold answer is a query, not a number, and a wrong unit is a type error rather than a plausible-looking figure. `PIVOT BY` (§7.39), `CLEAR` and `OPEN ON/CLOSE ON` are three verbs no other tool surface in the corpus exposes. The `.explain` / `.describe` shell commands are also the cleanest **schema-discovery ladder** we have seen for a query surface — the answer to "how does an agent learn the columns?" without dumping 10 tables into context. **GPL-2.0 — facts only.** |

Errors are a typed hierarchy (`FavaAPIError`, `FavaJSONAPIError`, `FilterError`, `ValidationError`, `EntryNotFoundForHashError`, `GeneratedEntryError`) each with its own `status` and a registered handler. `src/fava/core/` holds `filters.py`, `budgets.py`, `charts.py`, `conversion.py`, `ingest.py`, `tree.py`, `inventory.py`, `attributes.py`, `watcher.py`, `query_shell.py`. `src/fava/ext/` is a small extension API (`auto_commit`, `portfolio_list`). **MIT.** | 5.8 MB | The **read-and-write API layer over the deterministic engine** — i.e. the missing third piece that turns beancount+beanquery into something a mock can be shaped against. Two specific steals. (1) **Optimistic concurrency on every text write**: `put_source(file_path, source, sha256sum)` and `put_source_slice(entry_hash, source, sha256sum)` require the caller to send back the **sha256 of the version it read**, and `EntryNotFoundForHashError` is a distinct error type. That is a concrete, checkable answer to the read-modify-write race our `docs`/`sheets` mocks currently ignore, and it is a natural task ("two changes to the same file; the second must be rejected, not silently applied"). The core is `account_reconcile_oca` — `models/account_bank_statement_line.py` alone is ~1,340 lines of reconciliation state machine: `_default_reconcile_data`, `_compute_reconcile_data_info` / `_inverse_reconcile_data_info`, `_reconcile_data_by_model`, `_recompute_suspense_line`, `_check_reconcile_data_changed`, `reconcile_bank_line` / `unreconcile_bank_line` (each with `_edit` and `_keep` variants), `_auto_reconcile` / `_do_auto_reconcile(models)`, `_get_exchange_rate_amount` / `_compute_exchange_rate`, `button_manual_reference_full_paid`, `action_to_check` / `action_checked`, `add_statement`, `add_multiple_lines(domain)`, `_retrieve_partner`, `clean_reconcile`. Plus `account_reconcile_model_oca` (the matching-rule engine — see §7.42), `account_mass_reconcile` (`mass.reconcile.advanced` / `simple` + `mass_reconcile_history`), `account_partner_reconcile`, `account_reconcile_due_date`, `account_reconcile_wizard`, `account_reconcile_restrict_partner_mismatch` ("restrict reconciliation on receivable/payable when partners differ"), `account_reconcile_sale_order`, `account_reconcile_oca_queue`, `account_move_reconcile_forbid_cancel`, `account_statement_base`, `account_statement_reconcile_status`, `account_in_payment`, `base_transaction_id`, `account_move_base_import`. | 7.4 MB | **The most directly applicable repo in wave 3 for `bank_rec`.** Everything our family currently abstracts away is here as named, testable behaviour: a **suspense line** that absorbs the unexplained residual (so a partial match is a *state*, not a failure), `to_check` as a distinct disposition from reconciled/unreconciled, per-line **exchange-rate gain/loss computed at match time**, an explicit **un-reconcile** path with `_edit` vs `_keep` semantics (does undoing a match delete the counter-entry or leave it?), a partner-mismatch guard that refuses a plausible-looking match, and a **history table for mass reconciliation** so a bulk auto-match is auditable and reversible. §7.7 asked for un-reconciliation; this is the implementation. **AGPL-3 (mostly) — mine the state machine and the vocabulary, not the code.** |
| `oca-bank-statement-import` | https://github.com/OCA/bank-statement-import (branch 18.0 — `account_statement_import_base` is `"version": "18.0.1.0.2"`) | **18 addons**, AGPL-3 repo LICENSE (16 AGPL-3 / 2 LGPL-3). Two halves. **File import**: `account_statement_import_file` (the framework), `_camt` (ISO 20022 CAMT.053), `_camt54`, `_ofx` + `_ofx_by_acctid`, `_sheet_file` (CSV/XLSX with a configurable column map), `_sheet_html_file`, `_move_line`, `_file_reconcile_oca`, `account_statement_line_order`. Committed **test fixtures** for the parsers: `account_statement_import_ofx/tests/test_ofx_file/{test_ofx.ofx, test_ofx_iban.ofx, test_ofx_wrong.ofx}` and 14 CSV/XLSX fixtures under `account_statement_import_sheet_file/tests/fixtures/` — including `debit_credit.csv`, `debit_credit_amount.csv`, `multi_currency.csv`, `original_currency{,_empty,_no_header}.csv`, `balance.csv`, `empty_lines_statement.csv`, `sample_statement_en_empty_values.xlsx`, `sample_statement_offsets.xlsx` and `sample_statement_credit_card_inverse_sign_en.csv`. **Online pull**: `account_statement_import_online` (the provider base — `interval_type`/`interval_number`/`update_schedule`/`next_run`/`last_successful_run`, `statement_creation_mode ∈ {daily, weekly, monthly}`, `_pull(date_since, date_until)`, `_scheduled_pull()`, and dedupe on `unique_import_id`) with **six concrete providers**: `_plaid`, `_ponto`, `_gocardless`, `_paypal`, `_stripe`, `_wise`. | 5.3 MB | Closes the **front end of `bank_rec`**, which we had simply assumed away. Three things. (1) The fixture names *are* the trap catalogue: separate debit/credit columns vs one signed amount, a **credit card with inverted sign**, header offsets, empty values, multi-currency and an "original currency" column — each a real reason two people reading the same statement get different numbers. (2) The scheduled-pull object makes **feed freshness and idempotency** modellable (§7.43). (3) Six named aggregators (Plaid, Ponto, GoCardless, PayPal, Stripe, Wise) with different auth shapes is the sourced justification for a *multi-feed* bank story rather than one bank file. **AGPL-3 (mostly) — facts only.** |
| `oca-account-financial-tools` | https://github.com/OCA/account-financial-tools (branch 18.0) | **41 addons**, AGPL-3 repo LICENSE (37 AGPL-3 / 4 LGPL-3). The controls-and-closing suite: locking (`account_journal_lock_date`, `account_lock_date_update`, `account_lock_to_date`, `account_journal_restrict_mode`), fiscal calendar (`account_fiscal_year`, `account_fiscal_year_auto_create`, `account_fiscal_month`, `account_move_fiscal_year`), numbering and chronology (`account_move_name_sequence`, `account_journal_general_sequence`, `account_sequence_option`, `account_invoice_constraint_chronology`), fixed assets (`account_asset_management`, `_compute_batch`, `_force_account`, `_low_value`, `_number`, `_transfer`), deferrals (`account_spread_cost_revenue`), `account_move_template`, `account_netting`, `account_loan`, `account_cash_deposit`, `account_check_deposit`, `account_chart_update` (+ `_code_digits`, `_l10n_eu_oss_oca`), `account_partner_required`, `account_fiscal_position_vat_check`, `account_move_line_{purchase,sale}_info`, `account_move_line_tax_editable`, `account_maturity_date_default`, `account_move_post_date_user`, `account_payroll_sheet_import`, `account_dashboard_banner` (+ `_mis_builder`), `account_usability`. | 24 MB | The **controls vocabulary** we were missing (§7.45): five distinct locking mechanisms, a chronology constraint, and per-user post-date attribution (`account_move_post_date_user` — *who* posted it and *when*, separate from the accounting date). Also the only fixed-asset depreciation model in the corpus (`account_asset_management` + batch compute + transfers + low-value threshold), which is a straightforward exactly-verifiable arithmetic family we do not have, and `account_move_template` — recurring journal entries from a template, the natural home for §7.14's deferred-revenue schedules. **Honest caveat**: this is the least-mined of the five, and most of the 41 modules are small ergonomic patches with no research value. **AGPL-3 (mostly) — facts only.** |
| `oca-account-invoicing` | https://github.com/OCA/account-invoicing (branch 18.0) | **74 addons**, the largest of the five; AGPL-3 repo LICENSE (65 AGPL-3 / 9 LGPL-3). AR/AP invoice mechanics as one module per behaviour: discounts (`account_invoice_fixed_discount`, `_triple_discount`, `_global_discount`, `_discount_date`, `_discount_display_amount`, `account_force_early_discount`-adjacent), corrections (`account_invoice_refund_link`, `_refund_link_sale`, `_refund_reason`, `_refund_line_selection`, `account_menu_invoice_refund`), controls (`account_invoice_check_total`, `_tax_required`, `_supplier_ref_unique`, `_warn_message`), terms and dates (`account_invoice_date_due`, `_payment_term_date_due`), currency (`account_invoice_currency_by_partner`, `_show_currency_rate`, `account_manual_currency`), delivery (`account_invoice_transmit_method` + `_substitution_rule`, `_auto_send_by_email`, `_send_template`), plus `account_invoice_merge`, `account_billing`, `account_invoice_clearing`, `account_invoice_advance_compensation`, `account_invoice_supplierinfo_update`, `account_invoice_pricelist`, `account_invoice_custom_rounding`, `account_invoice_line_sequence`. | 14 MB | Moderate value, and the honest read is that it is **breadth, not depth**: 74 single-purpose patches, most of them UI or field-level. Three earn their keep. (1) `account_invoice_check_total` — a *declared expected total* that must equal the computed total before posting, i.e. an AP keying control that turns a transcription error into a refusal (a clean, exactly-checkable trap for our `ap_entry` shapes). (2) `account_invoice_supplier_ref_unique` — **duplicate-invoice detection keyed on vendor reference**, the single most common real AP exception and one we do not model. (3) `account_invoice_transmit_method` + `_substitution_rule` — invoices have a *delivery channel* (post/email/EDI/portal) with per-partner substitution rules, so "did it actually go out, and by what route?" becomes a checkable fact. **AGPL-3 (mostly) — facts only.** |
| `oca-account-payment` | https://github.com/OCA/account-payment (branch 18.0) | **24 addons**, AGPL-3 repo LICENSE (21 AGPL-3 / 3 LGPL-3). Payment execution and AR aging: `account_payment_return` + `_import` + `_import_iso20022` (**returned/bounced payments**, incl. an ISO 20022 return-file importer), `account_payment_multi_deduction` (one payment settling many invoices with per-line deductions), `account_payment_tier_validation` (**multi-tier approval on a payment**), `account_due_list` + `_payment_mode`, `partner_aging`, `account_payment_term_extension`, `account_payment_line`, `account_payment_method_base`, `account_payment_promissory_note`, `account_payment_credit_card`, `account_payment_notification`, `account_payment_show_invoice`, `account_payment_widget_amount`, `account_move_line_payment`, `account_check_printing_report_base`, `account_cash_invoice`, `account_refund_early_payment_discount`, `account_force_early_discount`, `payment_partner`, `payment_require_legal`, `account_voucher_killer`. | 5.9 MB | The **most valuable of the three "extra" OCA suites**, because it supplies the one thing §7.13 named as entirely unmodelled and could only source from an OpenAPI spec: **`account_payment_return` is a working implementation of a payment that settles and then comes back**, including a *file-driven* return import (ISO 20022 `pain.002`-family), which means the un-application and invoice re-opening are real code paths rather than a hypothesis. Add `account_payment_tier_validation` (approval tiers on the payment itself, not on the invoice) and `account_payment_multi_deduction` (partial settlement with deductions), and this repo covers the full failure surface of our `payment_proposal` and `cash_app` families. `partner_aging` gives an aging-bucket definition to check ours against. **AGPL-3 (mostly) — facts only.** |

## 9. Wave-3 acquisition method and running totals

**Method.** Same as waves 1–2: `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch`, then `rm -rf .git` (verified
absent at every depth under `repos/`). One repo was taken as a **partial clone**: `dolibarr`
(`--filter=blob:none --sparse` with a non-cone include list of `htdocs/api`, `htdocs/compta`,
`htdocs/fourn` plus the root loaders) — the full tree is a whole PHP ERP and only the REST API and
the accounting/supplier modules were wanted. Nothing else was modified, and no repo was pruned
after checkout. **All 19 requested repos landed**; nothing in the wave-3 list failed to clone.

Every claim in the wave-3 rows above was taken from the checkout — registration sites in code
(`server.tool(`, `@mcp.tool`, `@api_endpoint`, `@router.command`, `@url <VERB>`, `Route::`),
`__manifest__.py` / `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `composer.json` metadata, and `LICENSE` /
`COPYING` files — never from READMEs or directory names. Where a README and the code disagreed,
both numbers are recorded (`ai-books-mcp`, `stripe-agent-toolkit`, `plaid-mcp-server`).

**Wave-3 sizes on disk** (`du -sh`, largest first):

| Repo | Size | | Repo | Size | | Repo | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openbb` | 233 MB | | `oca-account-invoicing` | 14 MB | | `oca-account-reconcile` | 7.4 MB |
| `akaunting` | 58 MB | | `dolibarr` *(sparse)* | 6.9 MB | | `fava` | 5.8 MB |
| `stripe-agent-toolkit` | 26 MB | | `frappe-books` | 5.9 MB | | `beancount` | 5.4 MB |
| `finrobot` | 25 MB | | `oca-account-payment` | 5.9 MB | | `oca-bank-statement-import` | 5.3 MB |
| `oca-account-financial-tools` | 24 MB | | `bank-mcp` | 17 MB | | `ai-books-mcp` | 5.2 MB |
| `fingpt` | 24 MB | | `taxhacker` | 16 MB | | `beanquery` | 580 KB |
| | | | | | | `plaid-mcp-server` | 268 KB |

**Running totals.**

| | Wave 1 | Wave 2 | Wave 3 | Corpus |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Repos added | 24 | 16 | **19** | **59** |
| Disk added | ~600 MB | ~238 MB | **485 MB** | **1.3 GB** |
| Partial clones | 5 | 1 (`odoo`) | **1** (`dolibarr`) | 7 |
| Copyleft / restricted | 2 | 3 | **11** | 16 |

Budget status: the corpus is now **~2.2× the ≤600 MB budget** set in wave 1. The four named prunes
(`openbb` cassettes 140 MB, `erp-bench` `tasks_ui/` 107 MB, `odoo` i18n ≥153 MB, `akaunting`
`public/` 36 MB) total ~436 MB and would land it at ~880 MB with zero research loss; that is still
over budget, so the budget itself should be restated rather than pretended at. **Open risk carried
forward:** wave 3 more than doubled the copyleft share (11 of 19 repos are AGPL/GPL/BUSL), and
`akaunting`'s BUSL-1.1 is not an open-source licence at all — the "facts, not source" rule now
governs the majority of the corpus and needs to be enforced at review time, not just documented
here.
